prompt: Simplify the attached educational illustration substantially. Keep its forest-green ink, ivory paper, restrained burnt-orange and slate-blue graphic-novel screenprint look, with light halftone. Clean wide 16:9 composition. Remove all people, all hands, all patient anatomy and realistic diagnostic scans. Show ONLY: a simple ultrasound probe touching the top of a rectangular cutaway of TWO pale tissue regions separated by ONE clear horizontal boundary; a small connected monitor at the right. The tissue cutaway occupies the left two thirds, monitor the right third. Inside the upper tissue region draw exactly TWO thick straight parallel arrows: burnt orange pointing vertically DOWN from the probe to the single tissue boundary, with exactly one arrowhead at the boundary; slate blue pointing vertically UP from that boundary back to the probe, with exactly one arrowhead at the probe. These represent the outgoing sound pulse and the returning echo at different times. No arrows below the boundary, no extra arrows, no double-ended arrows, no waves or scattered starbursts. A single cable connects the probe to the monitor. On the monitor, show a simple horizontal baseline with just one small echo peak, not an anatomical scan. Exactly three small forest-green circular markers with cream numerals: 1 beside the orange downward arrow, 2 beside the blue upward arrow, 3 beside the monitor. No other writing, captions, titles, symbols, measurement labels or numbers. Lots of breathing room. Conceptual schematic, not to scale. Maintain very clear distinction between the arrow directions. This should be instantly understandable to a classroom student.
visual_review: Two unidirectional arrows: orange downward to one boundary, blue upward returning to probe; one echo peak; three matching live explanations. People removed. Detailed sourced four-step lesson preserved.
